items.evidence: The overview's first section is '## The bottom line' (line 3) with, in order, '**1. What FRUS answers directly.**' (line 5), '**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.**' (line 7) and '**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.**' (line 9); 'Scope', 'Decisions this needs from you' and '## Findings' (line 20) all come after. The collection's introductionText repeats the same three parts in the same order ('What FRUS answers directly: ... Where FRUS points for the rest: ... What this request cannot get from FRUS: ...').

Every count names its set and base: 'about one document in a hundred uses the vocabulary of corruption at all (3,174 of 311,429 documents), and about one in 650 does so three or more times (479 documents in 203 volumes)'; 'the 30 documents this overview cites; 28 of them carry a source line'; 'the pointed-at index covers 15 of those 20'; 'The library holds 483 dated documents from before 1860, in 9 volumes. A search for the corruption words returns 2 of them'; 'There are only 177 dated documents after 1989'; 'Watergate (183 documents in 51 volumes mention it)'; '18 of the 28 documents that discuss corruption at length in the 1890s'; 'of the 479 core documents, all 479 use a family word in some form and 419 use one of the five plainest'; 'in 35 (of 40) ... only 27 of 40'; 'about 6 documents in 100 in the ten volumes richest in it and 0.9 in 100 elsewhere ... "Department of State" ... 35 in 100 and 30 in 100 of the same two groups'. No bare percentage anywhere. The weakest instance is 'the rate per thousand dated documents was 1.2 to 3.5 in each decade from the 1860s to the 1900s ...', which names its base (dated documents, by decade) but not each decade's size. The remaining figures are dates, archival identifiers (Lot 91D414, entry A1 5403, NARA identifier 2131131; file numbers 893.00, 751K.00, 795B.00), ordinals ('where it appears fourth', 'the 21st-nearest neighbour') and a document's own reported sum ('Lockheed had admitted about $20 million in bribes abroad').

All 30 cited documents (I counted them against the collection: 30 document entries in 20 volumes, matching 'over the 20 volumes that hold the cited documents') are given in the printed form with a link, even on repeat, e.g. 'Foreign Relations of the United States, 1969–1976, Volume E–9, Part 2, Documents on the Middle East Region, 1973–1976, Document 161 (https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1969-76ve09p2/d161)', 'Foreign Relations of the United States, Diplomatic Papers, 1943, China, Document 202 (https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1943China/d202)', 'Foreign Relations of the United States, 1977–1980, Volume XIII, China, Document 94 (https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1977-80v13/d94)'. The two 1894 documents use the appendix's own printed numbering with the link: 'Foreign Relations of the United States, 1894, Appendix II, No. 7, Mr. Blount to Mr. Gresham (https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1894app2/d255)' and 'Appendix II, No. 23, Statement of Charles T. Gulick (...frus1894app2/d306)'. Descriptive back-references in the archival paragraph ('the Bunker telegram', 'the 1980 export memorandum') each point at a document cited in full elsewhere; nothing is cited by a bare id pair or by title alone.

The gaps are stated as searches with their terms and sets, and the principal one carries both controls: '(c) The period before 1860. The library holds 483 dated documents from before 1860, in 9 volumes. A search for the corruption words returns 2 of them, and a wider search that added the counterpart vocabulary of the period (peculation, defalcation, exactions, extortion, "presents to", irregularities) returns 49, which I did not read; the check that the search works found the phrase "Department of State" in 97 of the 483 and an impossible nonsense word in none. That is a gap in what is indexed, not evidence that early diplomacy was clean.' Likewise '(b) ... a search for the subcommittee's name, "Church", and "multinational" together returns 13 documents in 10 volumes' and '(d) There are only 177 dated documents after 1989 in the series as indexed, and none uses the corruption words; I make no claim about the 1990s', and '(e) Watergate (183 documents in 51 volumes ...), Teapot Dome (2 documents) or the Bank of Credit and Commerce International (1 document)'. One reservation: the post-1989 zero has no control of its own on the 177; its controls are the corpus-wide ones in 'How this was done' ('"Department of State" ... appears in 35 in 100 and 30 in 100 of the same two groups, and a nonsense word in none'). (a) is a reading limit bounded to 'the set' ('I did not find a document in the set that records a decision reversed on corruption grounds alone') and (f) is a statement about what the series is, not an absence claim.

No SQL, no table or column name and no file path anywhere in the overview. Volume and document ids occur only inside the history.state.gov links that J3 requires (e.g. '.../frus1969-76v06/d175'); never as a bare pair. The method is given in words: 'I dated documents by the date stored for each document, not by the volume year', 're-counting each occurrence in the flattened text of each hit document', 'the memo gives the distances against random pairs and against the typical 25th neighbour' (the memo is named, not pathed). The only identifiers are archival ones ('Lot 91D414, entry A1 5403, NARA identifier 2131131', 'file numbers such as 893.00, 751K.00 and 795B.00'). The collection file carries 'volumeId'/'documentId' fields, which are its format rather than the overview's text.

judge:s6.rankingReason: s6 first: the widest evidence (30 documents in 20 volumes read whole), the one measured decision effect the question asks for (Koreagate's lost House votes and the withdrawal timetable), a tested word family (35 of 40 against 27 of 40) that justifies the core set, and a collection with a note on every document, excerpts for the quotations and a threads-not-followed list; its costs are findings written as dense paragraphs and a 'where FRUS points' that reads as a wall of lot numbers. s2 second: 19 documents under six findings each framed as a decision (reluctance on aid, leverage on aid, policy reopened, alliance management, rules), scannable bullet quotations, the cleanest controls sentence ('Department of State' in 550 of 551 volumes and an impossible word found nowhere, in the same pass) and a read-next with threads whose documents are already identified; but it leaves out Koreagate and, by choice, the nineteenth century. s7 third: a clear five-role synthesis, the 1875 Venezuela case and the best-controlled 'cannot get' (kleptocracy with both checks), but it rests on only 11 documents in ten volumes, rounds its counts ('about 2,700', 'about 435'), gives one share with a vague base ('about two in five of the documents') and leaves several archival resolutions hedged ('or possibly to').

score:s6.notes: All four files present (memo.md, overview.md, collection.fruscollection, queries.log), plus the run's scripts and their outputs, which I read where an item depended on them. Re-verified on the read-only copy: the canary (553|321749|1103|8481), the 311,429 denominator, the 3,353 FTS inventory, N13's six counts, the pre-1860 figures (483 documents, 9 volumes, 97 positive control), the 177 documents of the 1990s, the header-only FTS (2 rows), 28 of 30 source rows and 5 of 30 external-citation rows, d249's 795B.00, d206's 1980-01-01, the two editions' d292 being byte-identical, and ten quotations as substrings of body_text. In the bundle: central-files-index.json resolves 91D414 -> 2131131 and 78D443 -> 619160 (matchType control), 79F80 is absent as the memo says, none of the seven lots is in lot-claimants-index.json, and the index, the shards manifest and the .generation file carry the same digest. The vector work is real (vec_setup.py, nbrs.py, mapops.py, neardup.py over semantic-vectors-binary.bin, the shards, semantic-map.bin), so V1-V6 and V8 were scored. Judgement calls, recorded so the adjudicator can weigh them: T1 is violated on one exploratory probe (`misappropriat` -> 0 in q1.out, 93 documents under the full word, never mentioned) against otherwise correct handling of the stemmer; R3 is kept obeyed because every null the memo reports is explicit and bracketed, though the same probe and an Abscam 0 (no output file) are silently dropped; P5 is obeyed on the literal share, with memo §1 restating N8's rates per 100 under an explicit pointer rather than the N of M; V1 is obeyed although the shards manifest itself was not read (every shard header was, and the manifest's digest is equal); V2's spot check is the Ed2-twin distance of 0 rather than a check on a multi-segment volume; P6's file-to-number map is complete for every count, with two inline JSON lookups (lot 67D586, lot-claimants) lacking an output file. O2 and O2' are split deliberately: every overview number traces to a memo line, but four number-words have no trace-table row. V4 and V5 are clear: the d292 neighbour list carries three Ed2 rows unsuppressed, and the core set's unclustered share is given against the corpus figure alone. V8 is clear in both the overview and two collection notes.

v7.memoClaimedStrict: memo §6, last paragraph: 'Documents in the overview reached through a vector operation and through no full-text query I ran: frus1948v07/d590 (the Cabot letter; the family regex gave it zero matches and the FTS inventory did not return it) and frus1969-76ve12/d222 (... my Lockheed full-text queries either required a co-term or only counted, so I reached it as a neighbour of d224; an unqualified search for Lockheed would also have returned it)'. The memo gives one list, not two readings; the overview repeats the claim ('reached two cited documents that way' and '"grafters", found only by the semantic search').
v7.evidence: Neither claim survives the strict re-run. frus1948v07/d590 is returned by `frus_documents MATCH 'scandal'` (queries.log line 25, q1.sh; the letter contains 'personal scandal'); the session logged that query as a COUNT(*) (606) and never listed its rows. frus1969-76ve12/d222 is returned by `frus_documents MATCH 'Lockheed'` (line 18, count 196; the memorandum uses 'Lockheed' five times) and by `MATCH 'scandal'` (line 25; 'the Lockheed scandal'); both were counts, and the id-listing Lockheed query at line 34 (q5.out) required a co-term and does not return d222. The memo's own hedge for d222 concedes the unqualified search; it makes no such concession for d590. In the practical reading both documents were first seen through the neighbour lists (nbrs1.out and nbrs2.out), so the overview's narrative of how they were found is accurate about the session's reading order but its 'through no full-text query I ran' and 'found only by the semantic search' are not true of the queries the log records.
